headline: Shallow 2029 slump, debt ratchets higher, blocs harden: a grinding, joyless half-decade

events: Ukraine front freezes into an unsigned ceasefire line; sanctions stay, reconstruction money trickles in
US extends Section 232 tariffs to more components; EU and Canada retaliate narrowly, China adds rare-earth licensing
Fed trims to 3.25% then pauses as core inflation sticks near 3%; ECB holds at 2%
AI capex boom continues; hyperscaler spending tops $600bn, power-grid bottlenecks delay data centres in Virginia, Ireland and Johor
Global growth ~2.9%; housing costs and insurance premiums dominate household complaints
US election produces divided government; a debt-ceiling standoff briefly pushes 10-year Treasury yields above 5.2%
Late-year oil spike on Red Sea/Gulf tanker incidents lifts G20 inflation back toward 3.9%
Ethiopia and Pakistan restructure under the slow Common Framework; Bolivia defaults
Japan's JGB 30-year yield breaches 3.5%, BoJ slows QT and Tokyo announces a consumption-tax-for-defence package
Corporate AI pilots convert to production at ~20% of firms; back-office hiring freezes spread in banking, insurance and BPO hubs
AI-equity correction (Nasdaq -28%) as monetisation lags capex; US slips into a shallow two-quarter recession
Global growth dips to ~1.9%; global unemployment peaks at 5.6%, youth joblessness surges in South Africa, Egypt and southern Europe
Fed cuts to 2.25%; stimulus is small because deficits already ~7% of GDP
Egypt needs an emergency IMF/Gulf rescue after remittance and Suez revenue shortfalls, the fourth sovereign crisis of the period
Venezuela-Guyana border clash escalates into a limited armed conflict over Essequibo, contained after US and Brazilian pressure
Recovery is tepid (~2.5%); firms use the downturn to lock in AI-driven headcount cuts rather than rehire
China pushes overcapacity exports of EVs, batteries and solar into the Global South; EU raises anti-subsidy duties again, Mexico and Brazil add tariffs
COP35 confirms the 1.5C threshold is effectively breached on a decadal basis; NDC updates are underwhelming
Record heatwave in South Asia and wet-bulb deaths in Pakistan fuel migration and climate-finance anger
Populist parties gain in France and Germany regional votes; EU fiscal rules quietly loosened for defence
World growth back near 2.7%, but per-capita income in much of Africa barely above 2019 levels
US debt passes 130% of GDP; interest costs exceed defence spending; bond vigilante episodes become routine but no crisis
Roughly a third of firms use AI in production; productivity gains visible in software, finance and logistics, not in services jobs
WTO dispute system remains dead; trade runs through overlapping bloc deals and minerals-for-security pacts
Renewables hit ~42% of power as cheap Chinese panels and batteries flood emerging markets despite tariffs in the West

winners: Leading AI and cloud firms that survived the 2029 correction with consolidated market share
Connector economies (Vietnam, Mexico, Gulf states, Morocco) arbitraging bloc rivalry
Owners of grid, power and critical-mineral assets
losers: Indebted frontier economies (Egypt, Pakistan, Ethiopia, Bolivia) squeezed by high rates and aid cuts
Young renters and entry-level white-collar workers in rich countries
Climate-vulnerable populations in South Asia and the Sahel
bullets: No collapse and no boom: global growth averaged ~2.6%, dented by a shallow AI-bubble-driven slump in 2029
Public debt crept to ~103% of world GDP; interest bills crowd out investment and every budget fight becomes a bond-market event
Tariff walls are higher and more numerous; trade has rerouted through connector countries rather than shrunk
AI is mundane infrastructure in a third of firms; ~48m jobs displaced cumulatively, concentrated in clerical, call-centre and junior professional roles
Inequality widened as capital and AI-owning firms captured gains while wages for routine cognitive work stagnated
Four sovereign debt crises were handled slowly and partially, leaving lost years across parts of Africa and South Asia
Warming reached ~1.58C; renewables grew fast on cheap Chinese hardware but fossil demand barely fell
Trust kept eroding and protest became chronic but diffuse: frequent strikes and cost-of-living marches, no revolutions
wildcard: A limited Venezuela-Guyana war over the oil-rich Essequibo region in 2029
image_description: In a sweltering 2031 Lahore evening, a laid-off call-centre worker delivers Chinese-made solar batteries by e-scooter past a shuttered bank branch whose window now advertises an AI loan assistant.
